_comment: The misconceptions Cambridge names for Stage 2, from TWO of the four Stage 2 books. Ids `<topic>-m<N>` come from the 'Common misconceptions' table in each of the 25 topics of the Teacher's Resource 2 (37 entries). Ids `rtg-NN` come from the 'Misconceptions' box in the Ready to Go Lessons (21 entries, of which 5 duplicate a Teacher's Resource row and 2 are deferred by Cambridge to a later stage - see _excluded). Ground truth for the misconception arm of science/lesson-kit/check-coverage.py. `misconception` states the false idea a child holds; `overcome` is this repo's one-line summary of the corrective move, not either book's wording. `lesson` is the Grade 2 standalone lesson that must answer it, resolved from which Stage 2 objectives that lesson actually carries.
source: Cambridge Primary Science Teacher's Resource 2 (Board & Cross), Common misconceptions, topics 1.1-6.3; and Cambridge Primary Science Stage 2 Ready to Go Lessons, Misconceptions boxes
_minimumCovered: Raised to the measured value when the depth pass lands; coverage is a number that only goes up.

_excluded._comment: Named by Ready to Go and deliberately NOT in this fixture, because Cambridge itself says Stage 2 is the wrong place. Answering them here would teach past the stage.
_excluded.a still object has no forces acting on i: Ready to Go: 'This will be addressed in Stage 5.'
_excluded.we see because of what our eyes do, rath: Ready to Go: 'will be explained in later stages to match learners' ages'
duplicates folded into the Teacher's Res: rtg 'a third set of teeth will grow' -> 4.5-m1
rtg 'the Moon gives off its own light' -> 5.1-m2

misconceptions.misconception: Habitat and environment mean the same thing.
misconceptions.overcome: An environment is the whole big area. A habitat is the particular place inside it where one living thing lives.

misconceptions.misconception: An animal's home, like a nest or a burrow, is its habitat.
misconceptions.overcome: The habitat is everywhere it needs: where it sleeps AND where it finds food and water.

misconceptions.misconception: Wild animals are only the dangerous ones, and they only live far away.
misconceptions.overcome: Birds, insects and fish near your school are wild too. Wild means it looks after itself, not that it is fierce.

misconceptions.misconception: A plant can grow anywhere.
misconceptions.overcome: A plant needs the right place. One that grows in a flower bed will not grow on a road or in the sea.

misconceptions.misconception: An animal can live anywhere, or in lots of different habitats.
misconceptions.overcome: Some animals need one exact kind of place. Move them out of it and they cannot live.

misconceptions.topicTitle: How can we care for our environment?
misconceptions.misconception: I am only one child, so nothing I do can help the environment.
misconceptions.overcome: One class of 30 not dropping litter is 30 people. A whole school is hundreds. It adds up fast.

misconceptions.misconception: Rock means a big heavy lump; a small piece or sand is not rock.
misconceptions.overcome: Rock comes in every size. Sand is rock broken into tiny grains.

misconceptions.misconception: Bricks and concrete are rocks.
misconceptions.overcome: People make bricks and concrete. You would not find them in a natural place unless somebody put them there.

misconceptions.misconception: You cannot push or pull something very heavy, or something fixed in place.
misconceptions.overcome: You CAN push a wall. You just cannot move it, because your push is not big enough. Pushing and moving are two different things.

misconceptions.misconception: A pattern has to be something you can see, like stripes or shapes.
misconceptions.overcome: Numbers make patterns too. Getting bigger every time is a pattern.

misconceptions.misconception: A moving thing slows down by itself, with no force needed.
misconceptions.overcome: Something invisible pushes back on it. Rub your hands together and feel the same force.

misconceptions.misconception: To move yourself one way, you must push that way.
misconceptions.overcome: You push the OPPOSITE way. Push back on a wall and you go forwards; your feet push right to turn you left.

misconceptions.misconception: Material means cloth.
misconceptions.overcome: Cloth is called fabric. Material means whatever a thing is made of - wood, glass, metal, rock.

misconceptions.misconception: The name of the object is the name of the material.
misconceptions.overcome: A spoon is the object; metal is the material. Ask what it is made OF.

misconceptions.misconception: If a material has been in a factory, it cannot be natural.
misconceptions.overcome: Some factories change a material's shape without changing the material. Cotton is still natural after the cotton factory, like wood is still wood after a chair is made.

misconceptions.misconception: Soft and smooth mean the same thing.
misconceptions.overcome: Soft means it squashes. Smooth means no bumps or holes. A sponge squashes and is full of holes.

misconceptions.misconception: Hard and strong mean the same thing.
misconceptions.overcome: Hard means it does not squash. Strong means it does not break. A plastic ruler is hard and snaps easily.

misconceptions.misconception: Brightly painted wood or metal is plastic.
misconceptions.overcome: Paint makes a thin shiny layer that looks like plastic. Look at a scratch, or a sharpened pencil, and you see the wood underneath.

misconceptions.misconception: A fabric is either waterproof or it soaks water up, one or the other.
misconceptions.overcome: Some fabrics are MORE waterproof than others, and even a waterproof one soaks up a little if water sits on it long enough.

misconceptions.misconception: Changing the shape of an object changes the material it is made of.
misconceptions.overcome: Roll paper into a tube and the tube is stiff - but unroll it and the paper is as bendy as ever. The OBJECT changed, not the material.

misconceptions.misconception: A human is not an animal.
misconceptions.overcome: In science, people are animals - a kind of mammal. Very different from the others, and still animals.

misconceptions.misconception: Older people are always taller than younger people.
misconceptions.overcome: People stop growing taller at about 17 to 20. After that they stay the same, and in old age may get a little shorter.

misconceptions.misconception: Boys get their features from their father and girls from their mother.
misconceptions.overcome: Everybody gets a mixture from both. Your eyes might be your father's and your hair your mother's.

misconceptions.misconception: A baby's features are the two parents' features mixed together and averaged.
misconceptions.overcome: Usually a baby gets one or the other, not a blend. A tall mother and a short father are more likely to have a tall or a short child than a middling one.

misconceptions.misconception: Eating healthily means never eating unhealthy food at all.
misconceptions.overcome: Your body needs a mixture of foods. The problem is eating too much of one kind, not eating any of it.

misconceptions.misconception: It does not matter if my baby teeth get damaged, because another set will grow.
misconceptions.overcome: Your adult teeth are already growing up inside your gums, where sugar can damage them before you ever see them. And that second set is the last one.

misconceptions.misconception: The light switch is the light source.
misconceptions.overcome: Look at where the light actually comes from. The switch only lets the electricity through.

misconceptions.misconception: Shiny things and the Moon are light sources.
misconceptions.overcome: They only bounce light back, like a mirror. A source MAKES its own light.

misconceptions.misconception: Darkness is the opposite of light.
misconceptions.overcome: Darkness is what is LEFT when there is no light. Take the light away and dark is what remains.

misconceptions.misconception: Darkness spreads out of corners and dark places, and creeps back again.
misconceptions.overcome: Nothing spreads. Add light and the dark goes; take light away and it is dark again.

misconceptions.misconception: The dark itself is frightening, because something might be in it.
misconceptions.overcome: Darkness is only a lack of light. Nothing is added when the light goes out - though you do have to move carefully, because you cannot see.

misconceptions.misconception: The Sun really travels across the sky.
misconceptions.overcome: The Sun stays still and the Earth turns. Spin slowly on a chair with your head still and the room appears to move past you.

misconceptions.misconception: Anything that works must use electricity, even a wind-up clock.
misconceptions.overcome: Look for a plug or a cell. No plug and no cell means no electricity.

misconceptions.misconception: Everything electrical is dangerous and must not be touched at all.
misconceptions.overcome: A torch or a toy with its cells covered up is made to be handled. Mains electricity is the dangerous one. Follow the rules and you are safe.

misconceptions.misconception: Electricity comes out of both ends of the cell and crashes together in the lamp to make light.
misconceptions.overcome: It flows one way round the whole loop, through the lamp and back to the cell.

misconceptions.misconception: The colour of the plastic on a wire changes what the wire does.
misconceptions.overcome: The metal inside is the same whatever the colour. Colour only matters in big complicated wiring.

misconceptions.misconception: Wires must be kept short so the electricity does not leak out.
misconceptions.overcome: Electricity cannot leak out of a wire. A long wire works exactly as well as a short one.

misconceptions.misconception: Tiny creatures like ants are too small to be real animals.
misconceptions.overcome: Most animals in the world ARE tiny. An ant is as much an animal as an elephant.

misconceptions.misconception: Grandparents are just old people, not your parents' own parents.
misconceptions.overcome: Your grandmother is your mother's or your father's mother. That is what makes her your grandmother.

misconceptions.misconception: A diet is something you go on to get thinner.
misconceptions.overcome: In science your diet is simply everything you eat and drink. Everyone has one.

misconceptions.misconception: You can see germs, so hands that look clean are clean.
misconceptions.overcome: Germs are far too small to see. A hand that looks perfectly clean can still be covered in them.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Ready to Go: the eggshell model
misconceptions.misconception: Because the eggshell went soft in a drink overnight, my teeth would too.
misconceptions.overcome: An eggshell is much softer than the outside of a tooth. The model shows what sugary drinks DO, not how fast.

misconceptions.misconception: The animals and plants in a place are there because people put them there.
misconceptions.overcome: They live there because that place gives them what they need. Nobody planted the moss or posted the beetles.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Ready to Go: similar and the same
misconceptions.misconception: Similar and the same mean the same thing.
misconceptions.overcome: The same means no difference at all. Similar means alike in some ways and different in others - which is what two animals usually are.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Ready to Go: natural and manufactured
misconceptions.misconception: Everything around us was made by people.
misconceptions.overcome: Wood, rock, wool and cotton were not made by anybody. They are natural, and people only shape them.

misconceptions.misconception: Toast is just bread with a brown surface, and the plain bread is still underneath.
misconceptions.overcome: The heat changed the bread itself. Break a piece open: it is toast all the way through, and you cannot turn it back.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Ready to Go: scientists and inventors
misconceptions.misconception: All inventors and scientists lived long ago and are dead.
misconceptions.overcome: Scientists are at work today, discovering things nobody knew last year. Some of them are quite young.

misconceptions.misconception: The little light in a circuit is called a bulb.
misconceptions.overcome: Scientists call it a lamp. Using the right word now saves confusion later, when bulb starts to mean something else.

misconceptions.misconception: A lamp will light if just one end of it is connected to the cell.
misconceptions.overcome: Electricity has to go all the way round and back. One connection is a gap, and a gap means no light.

misconceptions.misconception: Rocks, stones and pebbles are three different things.
misconceptions.overcome: They are all rock. The words just tell you how big the piece is and how smooth.

misconceptions.misconception: A shadow is a real thing, stuck to your feet and following you about.
misconceptions.overcome: A shadow is not a thing at all. It is the shape of the light that your body blocked.
